concepts.label: Administrator RBAC role
concepts.note: this is an RBAC role, a coarser-grained concept than the registered 'Query Manage Index' privilege; not the same concept, kept distinct

concepts.note: the version constraint below applies only to the replica-count-changing and replica-dropping actions of ALTER INDEX, not to the move action or the statement as a whole

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.evidence: Only users with the RBAC role of `Administrator` are allowed to run the `ALTER INDEX` directive.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.note: the registered requiresEdition predicate is defined for a clause/option within a statement, not the whole statement; this fact is about the entire ALTER INDEX statement's availability, so a new predicate was minted rather than misusing requiresEdition
relations.evidence: This directive is applicable only for Standard GSI (Plasma) and MOI Indexes; and hence supported only for Enterprise Edition nodes. (Not applicable for Forest DB.)

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.evidence: This statement is only supported only in Couchbase Server 5.5 and later; if the cluster is a mix of Couchbase Server 5.5 and previous versions, then this statement will not work.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index-replica-management
relations.evidence: In addition, altering the number of replicas or deleting an index replica is only supported in Couchbase Server 6.5 and later; if the cluster is a mix of Couchbase Server 6.5 and previous versions, then these operations will not work.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index-keyspace-on-syntax
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, you can use the index name with the `ON` keyword and a keyspace reference to specify the keyspace on which the index is built.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.note: distinct sub-fact from the replica-management version gate above: this one governs the USING clause / GSI-only index type requirement
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server 6.5 and later, the index type for a secondary index must be Global Secondary Index (GSI). The `USING GSI` keywords are optional and may be omitted.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.evidence: If you attempt to alter an index which is still scheduled for background creation, the request fails.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.note: structural link from an existing Markdown xref in the Related Links section
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, the _index redistribution_ setting enables you to specify how Couchbase Server redistributes indexes automatically on rebalance. Refer to [Rebalance](../../learn/clusters-and-availability/rebalance.md#rebalancing-the-index-service) for more information.

cross_product_finding.finding: This page leans heavily on self-managed-server-only concepts: an Enterprise-vs-Community edition split (Standard GSI/MOI/Plasma indexes are Enterprise-only) and a coarse RBAC 'role' (Administrator) rather than a fine-grained privilege. Capella has no 'editions' concept at all (it's a single fully-managed SaaS tier) and a different access model, so neither the requiresEdition-shaped fact nor the Administrator-role requirement would map cleanly onto an equivalent Capella page for index placement/rebalancing, if one exists.
